messages:
maria: heads up — after yesterday's prefetch rollout i'm seeing console chart frameskips and a few 5xx traces when kvcache is under pressure. noticed across canary and main. :grimacing:
ben: saw this too while trying the new heatmap. flamegraph points at main-thread GC spikes + large bundle parse. link: https://perf.redwood/reports/3891234567
noah: i pulled telemetry — there's a sharp spike in kvcache evictions at ~10:42 UTC and routing-policy shows a burst of requests pinned to eu-west-1-dense pool. could be eviction -> cold prefix hits -> long render.
emily: deploy-bot shows the prefetch feature flag flip at 10:40 and canary completed at 10:41. infra-bot: `deploy canary console-prefetch v2` succeeded. :eyes:
carla: interesting — did the rollout change route headers? our routing policy now prefers low-cost pool for background prefetches, maybe they collided with foreground requests.
maria: here's a short reproducer i used locally: `curl -H "x-redwood-route: prefetch" -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/console/query -d '{"q": "heatmap"}'` then open dashboard. reproduces ~80% of the time for me.
ben: adding that i see >200ms main-thread parse for the large widget script when kvcache miss occurs. bundling split didn't help — suspect runtime code path for replaying prefix cache is expensive.
noah: telemetry sampling might be masking some things. current sampling for console traces is 0.02, but heatmap has been excluded from high-sample buckets. i upped it to 0.2 for a minute and got more traces matching the GC+parse pattern.
emily: proposal: immediate partial rollback of prefetch flag for EU canary while we triage. we can revert via `featurectl rollback console-prefetch canary-eu`.
carla: also can we try a routing policy tweak — make prefetch requests use a separate pool with stricter concurrency (burst=10) so they don't steal capacity from rendering paths?
maria: agreed on both. i've opened an incident ticket: INC-2026-console-prefetch (link: https://inc.redwood/INC-2026). tagging @oncall. action items in the ticket: rollback eu canary, add isolated prefetch pool, increase trace sampling for 30m.
infra-bot: alert: rollback initiated by emily at 10:55 UTC. canary flag reverted.
ben: after rollback the cpu/parse tail dropped in the dashboard metrics. preliminary numbers look promising. i'll keep an eye for regressions.
noah: next steps — run a controlled replay: 1) run prefetch traffic against isolated pool, 2) stress kvcache to reproduce eviction pattern, 3) test incremental backfill for prefix cache to avoid heavy JS reparse.
emily: will schedule a quick sync 11:30 to decide long-term fix (pooling vs qps quotas vs bundle defers).
maria: thanks everyone. keep logs/links in INC-2026. :white_check_mark:
